overview: This Senate resolution states the Senate's view that the President already has legal power under existing immigration law to act immediately to secure the U.S.-Mexico border. It points to specific provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act that allow the government to suspend entry of foreigners, return some asylum seekers to Mexico while their cases are pending, and limit who can qualify for asylum. It urges the President and the Department of Homeland Security to use these powers, including bringing back the "Remain in Mexico" policy, detaining people who are not allowed into the country, ending the release of migrants while they await hearings, limiting humanitarian parole, using fast-track deportation, and ending taxpayer-funded benefits for people in the country illegally. As a "sense of the Senate" resolution, it expresses an opinion and does not itself change the law. As of January 21, 2025, a Senate committee had reported it and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say it makes clear that the executive branch can act now to control illegal crossings and protect public safety without waiting for new legislation.
against: Critics say the policies it urges, such as returning asylum seekers to Mexico and broad asylum limits, raise legal and humanitarian concerns, and that a nonbinding resolution does not resolve those questions.
